ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against: (a) FINTRAC's Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) list and domestic enhanced due diligence requirements under the PCMLTFR; (b) Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) and the United Nations Act; (c) Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) guidelines; (d) UN Security Council consolidated list; (e) U.S. OFAC SDN list and sectoral sanctions for USD-denominated operations via Mercury ACH and Stripe Billing; (f) conduct continuous real-time screening using a commercial AML screening database; and (g) maintain a risk-based enhanced due diligence file for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, or sanctions-flagged entity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry via AltaCorp (online corporate registry system operated by Service Alberta)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be in English or French, or a combination of both, using basic capital letters of the Roman alphabet, Arabic numerals, or certain punctuation. For names originating in non-Roman scripts, a statutory transliteration into the Roman alphabet is mandatory. The name must include a legal element such as 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC' (for an Alberta unlimited liability corporation) and must not be confusingly similar to any existing registered or reserved name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the Alberta Corporate Registry, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal or a revised name submission through the AltaCorp portal within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must cite the relevant provisions of the Alberta Business Corporations Act and the Corporate Name Regulation, and may include supporting evidence of distinctiveness, such as trademark registrations or trade name usage. A name reservation, once granted, may be extended for an additional 90 days before incorporation by filing a renewal request and paying the applicable fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are acceptable for the registered office requirement provided a physical street address in Alberta is designated as the registered office and the virtual office provider is authorized to accept statutory mail and legal process. However, for banking and payment processor onboarding (Stripe Billing, Mercury ACH), the beneficiary may be required to demonstrate a substantive operating presence; a virtual office alone may trigger enhanced due diligence or additional documentary requirements.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), as amended, Part 1.1 (Unlimited Liability Corporations, ss. 15.1–15.6) and ss. 11–13, 104, 110, 117 (incorporation, registered office, first directors); Corporate Registry Regulations, Alta Reg 186/2010.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry Division, Service Alberta / Registrar of Corporations under the ABCA (online portal: Alberta Corporate Registry OneStop).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Alberta) together with the NUANS Name Search Report, Registered Office Address Notification, and Consent to Act of First Directors; Certificate of Incorporation is issued upon approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account required for an Alberta ULC; incorporators may subscribe for common shares for nominal consideration without statutory paid-up capital constraints.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the subscription for shares by the incorporators be and is hereby approved, and the board authorises the issue of common shares for the aggregate consideration set out in the subscription ledger. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the registered office be established at 2000, 350 – 7th Avenue SW, Calgary, Alberta, T2P 3N9, and the Corporate Registry be notified accordingly. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the incorporators' proposed nominee be appointed as the first directors of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER: that such first directors appoint the President, Secretary and Treasurer, who are authorised to execute banking resolutions, open corporate bank accounts, register for a CRA Business Number and Alberta tax accounts, and execute annual return filings and ancillary documents as counsel may advise.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service Alberta Corporate Registry through a NUANS-accredited search house.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Procure a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report for the proposed corporate name in English or French; verify absence of confusing similarity with existing Alberta and other common-law Canadian names; apply for a 90-day name reservation through the Corporate Registry OneStop portal.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (dated within 90 days)
Consent letter from any third party whose distinctive name is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity, obtain a revised NUANS report with a new corporate name and resubmit; a reserved name may be renewed once for an additional 90 days upon Registry consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry Division, Service Alberta (Registrar of Corporations).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the prescribed ABCA Articles of Incorporation designating the entity as an Unlimited Liability Corporation, state the authorized share structure (e.g., unlimited common shares with or without par value), name the Alberta registered office street address, list the first directors, and include any restrictions on business if applicable; have each incorporator execute the Articles; attach the NUANS report, registered office notification, and signed director consents; file electronically through OneStop or physically at the Corporate Registry counter and pay the statutory fee.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act of the first directors
Notice of address of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a Notice of Deficiency or query, the incorporator may file amended Articles or a Clarification Statement within 15 days; once cured, the Registrar may backdate the Certificate of Incorporation to the original filing date absent third-party prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate Issuance, Organizational Meeting and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry Division, Service Alberta, in coordination with the directors and corporate secretary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Receive the Certificate of Incorporation and endorse its date on the Articles; convene an organizational meeting or execute unanimous written resolutions ratifying the first board resolution, adopting by-laws, approving the share subscription and issuance, appointing officers, and designating the corporate minute book; prepare share certificates and maintain the share register and register of directors at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Organizational meeting minutes or written resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains a clerical error, apply to the Registrar for a Certificate of Correction under ABCA ss. 13; the Registry re-issues a corrected certificate without additional substantive review, provided the error is clerical in nature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Division; Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC with the CRA for a Business Number (BN) and the applicable accounts: GST/HST account (RC-1), corporate income tax account (RC-1), and payroll account (RP-0001) if hiring employees; register the Alberta corporate income tax account with the TRA; for non-resident U.S. equity holders, prepare CRA Form T106 and document any 'check-the-box' election consistent with the corporation's unlimited liability character.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or TRA rejects an account opening, align the registered name and address exactly to the Certificate of Incorporation and resubmit with the directors' identification; if a U.S. investor election filing is deficient, file an amended election with a letter of explanation and pay any differential tax instalment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary Business Licensing Division or City of Edmonton Development Services (as applicable to the registered office).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a municipal General Business Licence application describing software publishing, DevOps tooling, and cloud infrastructure management; provide the certificate of incorporation, lease agreement, zoning compliance letter, and floor plan; obtain a change-of-use or occupancy permit for the office premises; complete fire and building safety clearance under the Safety Codes Act.
required_dossiers: Floor plan with proposed occupancy load
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality proposes refusal due to zoning or use restrictions, apply for a development permit variance or relocate the registered office to a permissible commercial zone; an appeal to the local Development Authority or Subdivision and Development Appeal Board may be filed within 21 days of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Annual Governance Maintenance and Registry Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (annual return); CRA and TRA (tax filings).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual return with the Corporate Registry within 60 days of each anniversary of incorporation; convene an annual general meeting or execute written resolutions in lieu under ABCA s. 110; file changes to directors, registered office, and share structure as they occur; maintain the corporate minute book and update the CRA business information as necessary.
required_dossiers: CRA and TRA tax return records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual return is filed late, pay the reinstatement/revival fee and, if the company was dissolved for default, apply for Revival under ABCA s. 209; the cure is normally available within one year of dissolution upon payment of all arrears and filing outstanding returns.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no provincial industrial licence is imposed on ISIC 6201 (software publishing / developer infrastructure) in Alberta; municipal licensing authority: City of Calgary / City of Edmonton Business Licensing Division.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business Licence (municipal administrative permit only; not a statutory industry licence).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — software publishing, database monitoring, and API cloud services have no stationary emitting source, effluent discharge, or physical works; an Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not required under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12, Schedule 2.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office operations must meet municipal stormwater and sanitary sewer bylaws; no industrial wastewater or VOC emission thresholds apply. If the company later owns or operates data centers, AEPA registration would be required for standby power generation and used electronic equipment would fall under the province's e-waste diversion regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain a fire inspection certificate from the municipal Fire Marshal verifying compliance with the Alberta Fire Code under the Safety Codes Act, including fire extinguisher placement, emergency lighting, and exit signage. Structural: provide a building occupancy certification confirming floor load capacity for any server racks or technical equipment. Occupational: register for a workers' compensation account with WCB-Alberta and adopt an Occupational Health and Safety program under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2 once employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); online portal: My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/account.html) and GST/HST NETFILE.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity obtains a federal Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1, Request for a Business Number, with the CRA; for GST/HST registration, Form RC20 or online Business Registration Online (BRO) is used. Non-residents must provide a Canadian address of a representative or authorize a registered Canadian agent. The CRA issues the BN immediately for online applications and within 5-10 business days for paper filings; an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) must also produce its Certificate of Incorporation from the Alberta Corporate Registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No direct check-the-box election under Canadian domestic law; however, for U.S. federal income tax purposes, an eligible ULC may elect under Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3 (Form 8832) to be treated as a partnership or disregarded entity, and the Canada-U.S. Tax Treaty (Article IV) may apply. Domestically, the ULC remains a taxable Canadian corporation subject to entity-level tax under the Income Tax Act; elections such as a closely related corporation election under Excise Tax Act s. 156 are available for GST/HST grouping.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under the Excise Tax Act; Alberta has no provincial sales tax, so the applicable federal rate is 5% GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide gross taxable supplies made in Canada (small supplier threshold), including digital services; non-residents carrying on business in Canada must register once this threshold is met unless they are exempt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal or Alberta mandate for real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or compulsory electronic invoicing. GST/HST invoices may be issued electronically in any format but must contain prescribed information under the Excise Tax Act (seller name, BN, tax amounts, and zero-rating reference). Electronic filing via GST/HST NETFILE is mandatory for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million; payments to the CRA above CAD 10,000 must be made electronically.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to a supply of intangible personal property (e.g., software, database access, API monitoring services) or a service made to a non-resident person, provided the supply is not made for use in Canada, is not in connection with real property situated in Canada, and is not a supply of a service rendered in Canada to a non-resident who does not have a Canadian business presence. Supporting evidence must establish the non-resident status of the recipient, the exported nature of the service, and that no Canadian adoption or use occurred.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years (or without time limit for misrepresentation), disallow the zero-rating, and charge the net GST/HST plus interest under the Excise Tax Act. A gross negligence penalty of 50% of the reassessed amount applies where the exporter knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence claimed zero-rating without substantiation. Fraudulent claims may lead to prosecution under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act, fines up to CAD 100,000, and imprisonment up to five years; correspondingly, any refund paid is clawed back with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has a fully convertible currency for both current and capital account transactions, consistent with IMF Article VIII. There are no exchange controls restricting capital inflows, dividend declarations, or profit repatriation by non-resident shareholders. However, distributions from a ULC to non-resident shareholders are generally subject to Canadian Part XIII withholding tax unless reduced by an applicable income tax treaty. All international electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more are reportable to FINTRAC, and banks must classify the economic purpose of each transaction for AML and sanctions screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion ratio on export receipts. A resident exporter may retain proceeds in any freely convertible currency, or repatriate and convert them at commercial bank rates. The only compliance requirements are standard invoicing, tax reporting, and FINTRAC large-transaction reporting for wire receipts of CAD 10,000 or more. No central bank approval is needed for holding offshore FX balances.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise Business, Payoneer, Mercury) can provide multi-currency disbursement rails and fast settlement for a low-risk DevOps cloud company, but they are not chartered Canadian banks and cannot hold demand deposits under the Bank Act. Such providers must be registered as Money Service Businesses with FINTRAC and maintain a Canadian agent for AML compliance. A Canadian ULC should maintain its primary operating account at a Schedule I bank and use an EMI only as a secondary FX disbursement rail for vendor payments where local clearing is faster.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally available for low-risk Alberta corporations, including non-resident-owned ULCs, because PCMLTFA permits risk-based electronic KYC. However, bank policy may require a physical or virtual interview for the authorized signatories if the ULC has a complex UBO chain or is owned by residents of non-treaty jurisdictions. Directors need not appear in person at an Alberta branch if they submit a valid board resolution, certified corporate registers, notarized passport pages, and proof of address. For higher-risk profiles, Canadian banks may mandate an in-person visit to a commercial banking centre, or a Canadian-qualified lawyer/accountant to serve as a notarizing intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO veil through a ULC with unlimited liability and no Canadian nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Registry certificate of incorporation; current annual return; complete ownership chart; certified corporate minute book; passport and proof-of-address document for every individual holding 10% or more beneficial ownership; corporate tax residency certificates; business plan and intended transaction profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial inbound capital injection exceeding CAD 100,000 from an offshore shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement; board resolution approving issuance of shares; evidence of allotment and filing of updated share register; source-of-funds statement; prior bank statements or asset vesting documents; FATCA and CRS self-certification forms; legal opinion on the absence of undisclosed nominee ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder or director residing in a FATF high-risk or monitored jurisdiction, or politically exposed person (PEP) status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence questionnaire; PEP declaration; independent legal opinion confirming legitimate source of wealth and funds; detailed organizational chart in trust or corporate structures; audited financial statements or asset evidence; certification that the ULC is engaged in genuine cloud infrastructure software operations in Alberta.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign shareholders remit equity capital by SWIFT MT103 into the ULC's named corporate account at an Alberta Schedule I bank. Canada does not require a foreign exchange approval or a dedicated purpose code; in the wire message the remitter should include the beneficiary's exact corporate name, the invoice or reference number, and the phrase 'Capital Contribution – Share Subscription'. For U.S. dollars, the bank will clear through its U.S. correspondent to Lynx (formerly LVTS) and convert or hold CAD as instructed. All incoming wires of CAD 10,000 or more must be internally documented by the bank for FINTRAC reporting. The ULC should retain the subscription agreement, share registers, and allotment minutes to support tax and treasury compliance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For services-based cloud infrastructure, API monitoring, and DevOps tooling, settlement should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for single high-value invoices and through Payments Canada's Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) or Real-Time Rail (RTR) for recurring domestic vendor payments. Commercial letters of credit are not appropriate for software subscriptions; they may be reserved for physical hardware procurement. For cross-border operational expenses, the ULC may use a FINTRAC-registered foreign exchange platform with settlement over Canadian correspondent banks, ensuring the final leg to the overseas vendor occurs through a Schedule I bank's SWIFT gateway.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward contracts (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR) with Schedule I Canadian banks against genuine commercial exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on illiquid or restricted emerging-market currency pairs
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term intercompany loans or convertible note facilities
Exchange-traded and OTC currency futures and options written by regulated Canadian or OECD counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return - Form AR-1 (corporate registration renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation; for example, an entity incorporated on 08 May must file its next annual return by no later than 07 July of that anniversary year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a CAD 100 late fee (approximately USD 74). A corporation that fails to file annual returns for two consecutive years is at risk of administrative cancellation or dissolution by the Registrar; reinstatement requires outstanding filings, applicable fees, and registry approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta corporate income tax administration, including all required ULC and ownership disclosure schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporate fiscal year-end; for a calendar fiscal year ending 31 December, the return is due no later than 30 June of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty under subsection 162(1) of the Income Tax Act: 5 percent of the unpaid balance owing plus 1 percent per complete month of delay up to 12 months. Late-payment interest and repeat-failure penalties also apply. Continued non-compliance may lead to CRA enforcement action and possible registry strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory audit applies to offering corporations under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. A non-offering ULC may dispense with an auditor for a fiscal year if all shareholders entitled to vote pass a unanimous shareholder resolution for that year. The exemption is lost if the corporation becomes an offering corporation, if shareholders holding at least 5 percent of the issued shares demand an audit, or if the articles require an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian reporting standards apply: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for publicly accountable enterprises, and Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private non-offering corporations. A Canadian ULC using U.S. tax check-the-box pass-through treatment still prepares Canadian statutory financial statements under the selected applicable Canadian framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta non-offering corporations must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) at their registered office and exercise reasonable diligence to identify ISCs. The register must be updated within 30 days after any share transfer or issue that changes significant control. Annually, the board reviews and confirms the ISC register and share register, and documentation is made available to Alberta Corporate Registry or law enforcement upon demand; no standalone annual UBO return is filed with the Registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute Book of shareholders and directors meetings
Register of share transfers and securities

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 250 - 750 US dollars per annum depending on agent and registered office location
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000 - 15,000 US dollars per annum for a certified review-level or full-audit engagement appropriate to a DevOps and developer infrastructure ULC
